messages.subject: interested but lost
messages.body_plain:
I have been trying for 2 days to create

a rackspace server (done)
SSH into it (done)
install R (done)
install Apache (done)
install RApache (not done)

As a newbie with limited technical skill left over from the 1990's, I get very lost very quickly

I have followed the following:

http://rapache.net/manual.html

But have no idea what anything means from : 3. Configuring rApache <http://rapache.net/manual.html#top> : onwards

I can run R from the command line and I can see the web server home page but I am no Apache specialist

If anyone would like to help me then please feel free what I am after is the following:

environment where I can build interactive R applications which can be accessed over the web and produce on the fly reports

I have compiled a shopping list

Rckspace Cloud server running Ubuntu
R (GoogleVis, Brew)
Apache
RApache
Wordpress
MySQL
Python

I actually fall down at the first hurdle as I dont really understand sys admin of hosted barebones server!

from these components I thought I could build a self contained environment for building these apps

Would really like some help

Jonathan

> On Saturday, March 9, 2013 2:22:27 AM UTC+5:30, Jeroen wrote:
> > The standard way of configuring Apache in Ubuntu is using config
> > includes. Usually you create a file
> >
> > /etc/apache2/mods-available/mod_R
> >
> > that contains:
> >
> > LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
> >
> > You can then enable or disable this module using
> >
> > sudo a2enmod mod_R
> > sudo a2dismod mod_R
> >
> > These command will create symlinks in /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/ which
> > are actually sourced by the main httpd.conf
> >
> > In a similar way, you can create a site, e.g to create a site 'rinfo':
> >
> > /etc/apache2-sites-available/rinfo
> >
> > that contains:
> >
> >  <Location /RApacheInfo>
> >       SetHandler r-info
> >  </Location>
> >
> > You can then enable/disable this site using:
> >
> > sudo a2ensite rinfo
> > sudo a2dissite rinfo
> >
> > After reloading rapache you should be able to visit http://localhost/RApacheInfo
>

messages.subject_clean: I am following the chapter instructions but can get no further with restarting Apache2 after install and config file changes
messages.body_plain:
The error message says that it cannot load /apache/module/path/mod_R.so because it cannot find it, not libR.so. Try looking in /usr/lib/apache2/modules or something, and then correcting the entry in your /etc/apache2/apache2.conf.

On Wed, Sep 11, 2013 at 2:07 PM, Jonathan Yates <jonathany...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Still slogging through chapter 3:
>
> trying to restart the server with the rApache mod in place
>
> jyates@socialjetrserver:/etc/apache2/mods-available$ sudo /etc/init.d/apache2 start
>
>  * Starting web server apache2
>
> apache2: Syntax error on line 271 of /etc/apache2/apache2.conf: Cannot load /apache/module/path/mod_R.so into server: /apache/module/path/mod_R.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
>
> Action 'start' failed.
>
> So followed the following from Chapter 3
>
> NOTE: When attempting to start apache2 on some UNIX systems, you may see an error message similar to this one:
>
> apache2: Syntax error on line 186 of /etc/apache2/apache2.conf: Cannot load
> /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so into server: libR.so: cannot open shared
> object file: No such file or directory
> To fix this, you will want to instruct your run-time linker, ld.so, on where to find libR.so. The easiest way to do this is by adding the directory to the /etc/ld.so.conf file and re-running ldconfig as root. If you don't know the location you can easily find out by running:
>
> $ R CMD config --ldflags
> -L/usr/lib/R/lib -lR
> In the output above, /usr/lib/R/lib is the directory you will want to place in /etc/ld.so.conf.
>
> Here is the file I updated as per the chapter
>
>  <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-ZbGBDZbgWqU/UjC-9Ikk_vI/AAAAAAAABGM/a-s2DEqqQxQ/s1600/Screen+Shot+2013-09-11+at+20.04.53.png>
>
> and here is the restart result:

messages.body_plain:
1: (slightly out of topic): I am very enthousiastic about rApache. It works like a dream. I will never use php anymore. Thank you!
2. I want to send a pdf file to the user. In the documentation is written that a png file is generated als follows:

setContentType("image/png")
t <- tempfile()
png(t,type="cairo")
plot(rnorm(10))
dev.off()
sendBin(readBin(t,'raw',n=file.info <http://file.info>(t)$size))
unlink(t)

Now I want to do the same with a (existing) pdf file. So I tried:
setContentType ("application/pdf")
temp <- "/var/www/limesurvey/tmp/o.pdf"
sendBin (readBin (temp, 'raw', n=file.info <http://file.info>(temp)$size))

But this does not work. Probably the headers are incorrect.
Does anyone know how this can be done?
Thanks
Frans Marcelissen
(fransiepan...@gmail.com)

messages.subject: Re: download pdf
messages.body_plain:
Thank  you for the answer. I still do'nt understand what to do.
I want that the user is asked where he should load the file.
Under php this can be done as follows:

header("Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=" . urlencode($file));
header("Content-Type: application/octet-stream");
header("Content-Type: application/download");
header("Content-Description: File Transfer");
header("Content-Length: " . filesize($file));

Under r the (full) file is as follows:

setContentType ("application/pdf")
temp <- "/tmp/o.pdf"

sendBin (readBin (temp, 'raw', n=file.info <http://file.info>(temp)$size))

You can see the result at http://www.dpvragenlijst.nl/loadpdf.r

The result is that (under firefox) the file is downloaded as "loadpdf.r". Under internet exporer the content is displayed in the browser. Both is not what I want.
I suppose, in order to do the same as under php the other header lines should be specified as well. My question is: how can I do that under r/rapache?
Thanks
--------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Re: how to configure Rapache
messages.body_plain:
As i had no previous experience with using R in this context, i misunderstood the example as well at first.
It's actually an example of how to combine the brew package with rApache. You have to install the brew package
and add a handler for brew in your config, that runs the brew function over the file containing the code.
Example from the official documentation to add to your config:

<Directory /var/www/brew>
    SetHandler r-script
    RHandler brew::brew
</Directory>

If a file from the /var/www/brew folder is called by the browser, rApache will execute the brew() function from the brew package with this file as input.
The output includes the evaluation from everything between the <%%>. For more information, check ?brew if you have the package installed.

Best of luck,
Z
